text: Earlier dev-split runs tested `GAMMA` across `{0.25, 0.5, 1.0}` at `(YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.35, P_SPEED=0.1, stop_gate=True)` and `P_SPEED` across `{0.03, 0.1}` at `(GAMMA=0.25, YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.2, stop_gate=True)`, showing a consistent trade-off between narrower 90% bands and lower `EB BTH->MLE` coverage. Only `GAMMA=0.1` remains untried to complete the full allowed `GAMMA` sweep `{0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0}` at `(YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.35, P_SPEED=0.1, stop_gate=True)`, and only `P_SPEED=0.01` remains untried to complete the full allowed `P_SPEED` sweep `{0.01, 0.03, 0.1}` at `(GAMMA=0.25, YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.2, stop_gate=True)`. Testing those two configurations will verify whether strong tempering at `YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.35, P_SPEED=0.1` inflates band width and degrades error relative to `GAMMA=0.25`, and whether restricting speed transitions (`P_SPEED=0.01`) at `YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.2` further narrows bands below `52.0 m` at the cost of deeper `EB BTH->MLE` under-coverage.

args.refuted_if: band_width_mean_m <= 87.0, or coverage_mean <= 0.941, or EB BTH->MLE coverage <= 0.863, or error_delta_ci_m upper bound <= 0, or accepted is true.
args.rationale: Completing the GAMMA sweep {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} at YAW_SD_FLOOR=0.35, P_SPEED=0.1, stop_gate=True by lowering GAMMA from 0.25 to 0.10 flattens the yaw-rate likelihoods; we predict band_width_mean_m will exceed 87.0 m, coverage_mean will exceed 0.941, EB BTH->MLE coverage will exceed 0.863 (keeping coverage_ok true), and error_delta_ci_m upper bound will be > 0, resulting in accepted=false.
